prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1045; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the first notice of loss for the left-turn collision. Insured reports the other vehicle entered the intersection on a green light and struck the rear quarter panel as insured's vehicle was completing the turn. Police report requested. No citations were noted at the scene.

Entry 2: Spoke with the insured by phone. Insured confirms they checked oncoming traffic before turning and saw no approaching vehicle in the near lane. Insured has a photo of the damaged passenger-side door and a dashcam clip that is being retrieved. Rental coverage explained and accepted.

Entry 3: Claimant is now represented by counsel. All contact to be routed through the attorney's office going forward. Received a letter of representation and a preliminary demand package that lists neck pain and headaches following the collision. Medical records requested under signed authorization.

Entry 4: Reviewed the physical damage estimate from the appraiser. Vehicle is repairable. Shop has flagged a possible hidden frame issue on the rear bumper bracket, so a supplement is expected. Coverage confirmed under the collision section of the policy, subject to deductible.

Entry 5: Received treatment records from the claimant's chiropractor showing a diagnosis of cervical strain consistent with whiplash, with a plan of physical therapy over several weeks. Records reviewed against the reported mechanism of injury and the photos of the vehicles. Injury evaluation remains open pending the physician's follow-up notes and the attorney's itemized specials.
